# decern

> A deterministic authorization decision point, in Rust. decern answers whether an agent, a person or a workload may do something, now. It proves its safety rules hold across the whole model with the cvc5 solver (not by sampling), records every decision in an Ed25519-signed, hash-chained ledger before it is served, and lets the party a decision was about verify and challenge it. Apache-2.0.

decern fills a gap decide-only policy engines leave open: a decision you can prove, record and contest. It is the reference implementation of a contestability layer for authorization — who a decision is about (decision-subject), who is answerable for it (operator-of-record), and how it is contested (the subject-side challenge, S-ARAP) — built on profiles authored in the IETF and the OpenID AuthZEN Working Group. Built and maintained by Anivar A. Aravind (https://anivar.net).

## Pages
- [Home](https://decern.anivar.net/): what decern is, how it works, an interactive protocol explorer that steps through how a caller is established under each of the five postures (bearer, signed-request, SPIFFE, AAuth, trusted front) and what happens to the request, the contestability triad, the architecture, and how to run it.

## Standards decern implements
- AuthZEN 1.0 (OpenID): the authorization API surface — single and batch evaluation, search, discovery.
- Caller postures: RFC 9068 bearer tokens, RFC 9421 signed requests, SPIFFE JWT-SVID, draft-hardt-oauth-aauth-protocol-11 agent tokens, or a declared authenticating front.
- Contestability profiles (authored by Anivar Aravind): draft-aravind-oauth-decision-subject, draft-aravind-oauth-operator-of-record, and the Subject-Side Access Challenge Profile (S-ARAP) in the OpenID AuthZEN WG.
- Ledger: Ed25519 (RFC 8032), Certificate Transparency Merkle tree (RFC 9162), JSON Canonicalization Scheme (RFC 8785).

## What decern is not
decern decides and records; it does not enforce, issue credentials, or run approval UX. It is not a gateway, a firewall for tool calls, or an authorization server.
